A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how the pharmaceutical industry is a dynamic industry in terms of the introduction of new products.

we have found evidence that supports the notion that the ability of firms to sustain above-average performance is related to their innovative capabilities, but that it does not appear to be related to their ability to avoid competition.
the pharmaceutical industry has been a highly innovative industry, with new products being introduced at an increasing rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pharmaceutical industry is not a "winner-take-all" industry.
innovation is a critical component in the persistence of superior profitability in the pharmaceutical industry.
the ability of a pharmaceutical firm to sustain superior profitability is not simply a function of the firm's innovative prowess, but also of the firm's ability to avoid competition from rivals.
